# Week 5 Deload Programme

**Client Profile:** Advanced male, 26, transitioning out of a 4-week high-volume hypertrophy block (18 working sets/session, RPE 8.5) into a deload before an intensification phase.

**Deload Strategy:**
- **Volume:** Reduce working sets by ~50% (from 18 → 9 working sets/session)
- **Intensity:** Drop RPE from 8.5 → 6 (roughly 4 reps in reserve on every set)
- **Load:** Use approximately 65–70% of the loads used at RPE 8.5 in Week 4
- **Tempo:** Controlled eccentrics (2–3 sec down), no grinding reps, no failure
- **Frequency:** Same 4-day split, same exercises — preserve neural patterning while clearing systemic fatigue
- **Bar speed:** Every rep should feel crisp. If it doesn't, drop the load further.

---

## Day 1 — Lower (Quad Focus)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Back Squat | 3 × 5 | 65% / RPE 6 | Smooth, controlled; no belt unless habitual |
| Romanian Deadlift | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 | Light stretch, leave the bar floating |
| Leg Press | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 | Half the usual stack work |
| Walking Lunges | 1 × 8/leg | Light DBs | Movement quality only |
| Leg Extension | 1 × 10 | RPE 6 | Pump set, no grind |

**Total working sets: 9**

---

## Day 2 — Upper (Push Focus)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bench Press | 3 × 5 | 65% / RPE 6 | Crisp lockouts |
| Overhead Press | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 | Strict, paused on chest if normally done |
| Incline DB Press | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 | Controlled tempo |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 1 × 12 | RPE 6 | Pump only |
| Triceps Pushdown | 1 × 12 | RPE 6 | Pump only |

**Total working sets: 9**

---

## Day 3 — Lower (Posterior Chain Focus)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conventional Deadlift | 3 × 3 | 65% / RPE 6 | Reset every rep, no touch-and-go |
| Front Squat | 2 × 5 | RPE 6 | Upright, clean reps |
| Hip Thrust | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 | Slow eccentric |
| Seated Leg Curl | 1 × 10 | RPE 6 | Pump |
| Standing Calf Raise | 1 × 12 | RPE 6 | Pump |

**Total working sets: 9**

---

## Day 4 — Upper (Pull Focus)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weighted Pull-Up | 3 × 5 | RPE 6 | ~50% of usual added load |
| Barbell Row | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 | Strict, no body english |
| Chest-Supported DB Row | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 | Controlled |
| Face Pull | 1 × 12 | RPE 6 | Pump, posture work |
| Hammer Curl | 1 × 12 | RPE 6 | Pump |

**Total working sets: 9**

---

## Programming Notes for the Trainer

- **Warm-ups stay normal.** Don't strip those out — they're part of the movement prep, not the fatigue.
- **No accessory finishers, no drop sets, no AMRAPs.** If the client is the type who wants to "push it" because he feels fresh by Day 3, hold the leash.
- **Cardio:** Cut conditioning by half. Low-intensity only (zone 2, 20–30 min, 2× this week max).
- **Sleep target:** 8+ hours. This is where the deload actually happens.
- **Nutrition:** Maintain calories at maintenance — don't cut, even though training stress drops. Protein stays at 1.8–2.2 g/kg. Slight reduction in carbs (10–15%) is fine given lower output, but only if the next block is hypertrophy/intensification rather than strength-led.
- **Recovery adjuncts:** Soft tissue work, mobility, sauna if available. Skip ice baths in the 24 hours post-session — blunts adaptation signalling, which matters less here but the habit is worth keeping.

## Readiness Check Before Week 6

By end of Week 5, the client should report:
- Joints feel "quiet" (no nagging elbows, knees, shoulders)
- Sleep quality improved
- Sessions feel almost *too easy* — that's the point
- Resting HR trending down 3–5 bpm if tracked

If those boxes tick, he's primed to open the intensification block hard. If not, extend the deload by 3–4 days before ramping back up.

Good catch — let me work off the actual numbers you gave me rather than the round figure I used.

## Week 4 (Last Week) Working Volume

You said **18 working sets/session at RPE 8.5** across compounds. Over a 4-day split that's:

| Day | Week 4 Working Sets |
|---|---|
| Day 1 — Lower (Quad) | 18 |
| Day 2 — Upper (Push) | 18 |
| Day 3 — Lower (Posterior) | 18 |
| Day 4 — Upper (Pull) | 18 |
| **Weekly total** | **72 working sets** |

## Deload Targets (Week 5)

Standard deload literature (Israetel, Helms) supports **40–60% volume reduction** combined with intensity drop when coming off a high-RPE accumulation block. Given he was at RPE 8.5 for 4 weeks — that's real systemic fatigue — I'd push toward the lower end of volume retention.

**Target: 50% volume cut → 9 working sets/session, 36 weekly.**

| Day | Week 4 Sets | Week 5 Sets | % Reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 — Lower (Quad) | 18 | 9 | –50% |
| Day 2 — Upper (Push) | 18 | 9 | –50% |
| Day 3 — Lower (Posterior) | 18 | 9 | –50% |
| Day 4 — Upper (Pull) | 18 | 9 | –50% |
| **Weekly total** | **72** | **36** | **–50%** |

## Intensity Targets

| Metric | Week 4 | Week 5 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compound RPE | 8.5 | 6.0 | –2.5 RPE |
| Reps in reserve | ~1.5 | ~4 | +2.5 RIR |
| Working load (% of Wk 4 top set) | 100% | 65–70% | –30–35% |

## Quick Sanity Check on the Numbers

- **Sets reduction:** 50% — aggressive enough to clear fatigue, conservative enough to maintain neural patterning and muscle stiffness.
- **Load reduction:** A drop from RPE 8.5 to RPE 6 at the same rep count corresponds to roughly a 30% load reduction in trained lifters (using Helms' RPE chart). So 65–70% of Week 4 load lands him at RPE 6 cleanly.
- **Combined stimulus:** ~50% volume × ~67% load ≈ **roughly one-third of Week 4's total tonnage.** That's the deload sweet spot for an advanced lifter going into intensification — enough to maintain, not enough to fatigue.

The session-by-session prescription I gave in the previous message already matches these targets (9 working sets/day, RPE 6 across the board, 65% loads on the main lifts). So the programme stands — but now you've got the math behind it if he asks why the drop is exactly where it is.

Want me to also map the **expected loads** session by session if you give me his Week 4 top-set weights on the main lifts (squat, bench, deadlift, OHP, pull-up)?

Good call — deload week is exactly when you address that, not the intensification block.

## Swap: Barbell Bench → Football Bar (Swiss Bar) Press

If your gym has a football/Swiss bar, that's the first-choice swap. Neutral grip drops shoulder external rotation demand significantly, keeps the press pattern intact, and lets him still load the chest meaningfully.

**If no Swiss bar available, use:** Flat Dumbbell Press, neutral grip (palms facing). Same principle — neutral grip, free range of motion, lets the shoulder find its own groove rather than locking it into the barbell's fixed path.

## Updated Day 2 — Upper (Push Focus)

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Load / RPE | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Swiss Bar Press** (or Neutral-Grip DB Press) | 3 × 5 | RPE 6 | Neutral grip, controlled descent, stop 1–2" off chest if full ROM provokes |
| Overhead Press | 2 × 6 | RPE 6 | **Reassess — see note below** |
| Incline DB Press (neutral grip) | 2 × 8 | RPE 6 | Switch from pronated to neutral; 30° incline max |
| Cable Lateral Raise | 1 × 12 | RPE 6 | Pump only |
| Triceps Pushdown | 1 × 12 | RPE 6 | Pump only |

**Total working sets: 9** (volume target preserved)

## Why These Substitutions Work

- **Swiss bar / neutral DB:** Neutral grip reduces anterior capsule stress and lets the humerus track in a more shoulder-friendly path. Most cranky-bench lifters tolerate this with zero symptoms.
- **Incline DB neutral grip:** Same logic. Removes the pronated-grip + flared elbow combo that usually flares benching shoulders.
- **30° incline cap:** Steeper inclines load the anterior delt more and re-introduce the impingement-y position you're trying to avoid.

## Flag on Overhead Press

If his shoulder is cranky benching, **OHP may also be irritating** — especially behind-the-neck or strict barbell variations. I'd ask him directly this week:

- **If OHP is symptom-free:** Keep as written.
- **If there's any pinch or ache:** Swap to **Landmine Press** (2 × 6, RPE 6) or **Neutral-Grip Seated DB Press**. Both keep the vertical press pattern without forcing full overhead external rotation.

## Diagnostic Use of This Week

Deload is the perfect window to test what aggravates and what doesn't, because loads are low and you've got recovery capacity. Have him log:

- Pain/pinch location (front of shoulder? top? AC joint?)
- Which positions provoke (bottom of bench? lockout? overhead?)
- Whether warm-up resolves it or it persists

That intel shapes the intensification block. If the Swiss bar / neutral DB feels clean all week, you've got your bench substitute for Weeks 6–9. If symptoms persist even on neutral-grip work, he needs assessment before loading heavy again — don't open intensification on a shoulder that's still talking.

Want me to build a short pre-press shoulder prep sequence (5 min, banded + scap work) to run before Day 2 and Day 4?

## Mobility Session — Day 5 (or Day 6)

**Placement:** Slot it on **Day 5** (the day after the Day 4 pull session) or **Day 6** if he prefers a full rest day after Day 4. Avoid stacking it on a training day during deload — the point is to give the nervous system a low-stimulus day, not add a session to a training day.

**Format:** 20 minutes, flow-style, breath-led. No PRs, no end-range loading, no "earn it" mentality. Think of it as a long warm-up with no workout attached.

---

## The Session

### Block 1 — General Movement Prep (5 min)

| Drill | Duration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Cat-Cow | 60 sec | Slow, breath-paced |
| World's Greatest Stretch | 60 sec/side | Full rotation, reach long |
| 90/90 Hip Switches | 90 sec | Smooth transitions, no forcing |
| Bear Crawl (slow) | 60 sec | Controlled, opposite limb |

### Block 2 — Shoulder Focus (6 min) *(prioritised given the cranky bench)*

| Drill | Duration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Banded Pass-Throughs | 90 sec | Light band, wide grip, no pinch |
| Wall Slides (forearm to wall) | 90 sec | Scap upward rotation focus |
| Thread the Needle | 60 sec/side | T-spine rotation |
| Prone Y-T-W | 90 sec | Light, slow, hold each letter 2 sec |

### Block 3 — Hips & T-Spine (6 min)

| Drill | Duration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Couch Stretch | 90 sec/side | Hip flexor length, no cranking |
| Deep Squat Hold w/ Pry | 90 sec | Sit in, gently rotate knees out |
| Half-Kneeling T-Spine Rotation | 60 sec/side | Hand behind head, rotate to ceiling |
| Adductor Rock-Backs | 60 sec | Side-lying or quadruped |

### Block 4 — Downregulation (3 min)

| Drill | Duration | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Supine 90/90 Breathing | 3 min | Feet on bench, ribs down, exhale fully through pursed lips |

---

## Programming Notes

- **Intensity cue:** Every position should feel like a 4/10 stretch — never a 7. If he's gritting his teeth, back off.
- **Breathing:** Nasal in, slow exhale. The downregulation block isn't optional — it's the parasympathetic signal that closes out the deload week.
- **Shoulder caveat:** If any drill provokes the cranky shoulder (especially pass-throughs or Y-T-W), skip it. Don't push through pain on a diagnostic week.
- **Optional add-on:** 10 min easy walk before or after. Sunlight if available.

## Updated Week 5 Layout

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Day 1 | Lower (Quad) — 9 sets, RPE 6 |
| Day 2 | Upper (Push) — Swiss bar swap, 9 sets, RPE 6 |
| Day 3 | Lower (Posterior) — 9 sets, RPE 6 |
| Day 4 | Upper (Pull) — 9 sets, RPE 6 |
| **Day 5** | **Mobility — 20 min** |
| Day 6 | Full rest (optional zone 2 walk, 20–30 min) |
| Day 7 | Full rest — prep for Week 6 intensification |

This keeps total weekly stress low, gives the shoulder a structured input without loading it, and finishes the week with two clean rest days before he opens the next block.

## Zone 2 Cardio — 2× This Week, 30 min Each

**Intensity target:** True Zone 2 — roughly **60–70% of max HR**, or the "nose-breathing / hold a conversation in full sentences" pace. If he's panting or needs to mouth-breathe, he's drifted into Zone 3 and is adding fatigue rather than aiding recovery.

**Modality:** Anything low-impact and rhythmic — bike (preferred), incline walk on treadmill, rower at low stroke rate, or outdoor walk. **Avoid running** this week — unnecessary joint load during a deload.

**RPE check:** 3–4/10. He should finish feeling *better* than when he started.

## Placement in the Week

The goal is to space cardio away from lower-body sessions (so it doesn't compound leg fatigue) and away from the mobility/rest days (so we preserve true recovery days).

| Day | Session | Cardio? |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Lower (Quad) | — |
| **Day 2** | Upper (Push) | **+ Zone 2, 30 min** (post-session or PM) |
| Day 3 | Lower (Posterior) | — |
| **Day 4** | Upper (Pull) | **+ Zone 2, 30 min** (post-session or PM) |
| Day 5 | Mobility — 20 min | — |
| Day 6 | Full rest | — |
| Day 7 | Full rest | — |

## Why This Placement

- **Pairs with upper days:** Legs stay fresh between Day 1 and Day 3, and Day 3 and the next block opener.
- **Same-day stacking is fine at this intensity:** Zone 2 at 30 min won't interfere with the upper session's recovery — it actually aids blood flow and clearance.
- **PM session if separate:** If he prefers splitting them, AM lift / PM cardio (6+ hours apart) works well. Don't do cardio *before* the lift.
- **Day 5 stays mobility-only:** Don't bolt cardio onto the mobility day — that day's job is downregulation, not output.
- **Days 6 & 7 stay clean:** Two genuine rest days before opening intensification. If he's restless, a 20–30 min easy walk is fine but not prescribed.

## Quick Cues for Him

- **Bike:** Keep cadence 80–90 rpm, low resistance.
- **Incline walk:** 3–4 mph at 5–8% incline usually lands most lifters in Zone 2.
- **Rower:** 20–22 strokes/min, light pressure.
- **HR cap:** If he tracks, **roughly 130–140 bpm** for a 26-year-old male (estimated max HR ~194; 70% ≈ 136). Adjust to his actual data if he has it.

## Final Week 5 Layout

| Day | Session | Volume / Stimulus |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Lower (Quad) | 9 sets, RPE 6 |
| Day 2 | Upper (Push) + Zone 2 30 min | 9 sets, RPE 6 + low aerobic |
| Day 3 | Lower (Posterior) | 9 sets, RPE 6 |
| Day 4 | Upper (Pull) + Zone 2 30 min | 9 sets, RPE 6 + low aerobic |
| Day 5 | Mobility | 20 min, RPE 3 |
| Day 6 | Rest | Optional easy walk |
| Day 7 | Rest | Prep for Week 6 |

**Weekly totals:** 36 working sets, 2 × Zone 2, 1 × mobility, 2 full rest days. That's a clean deload — fatigue clears, patterns stay grooved, engine ticks over, shoulder gets diagnostic information, and he opens Week 6 primed.

Good instinct from him, but the framing matters: **deload week is for tracking *readiness*, not testing *strength*.** A true 1RM or AMRAP test re-introduces the systemic fatigue you're spending the week clearing. That said, there are clean ways to get useful strength-adjacent data without breaking the deload.

## What to Track (Deload-Safe)

### 1. Bar Speed on Top Set of Main Lifts
**Where:** Day 1 Squat, Day 3 Deadlift, Day 4 Pull-Up (skip bench given the shoulder).
**Protocol:** On the top working set (3 × 5 at 65%), film from the side and measure mean concentric velocity, or just eyeball rep speed.
**What it tells you:** At 65% of Week 4 loads, those reps should move noticeably faster than they did at the same absolute load in Week 4. If they don't, fatigue isn't clearing — extend the deload.
**Cost to recovery:** Zero. He's lifting these loads anyway.

### 2. Grip Strength (Hand Dynamometer)
**Where:** Day 1 morning and Day 7 morning.
**Protocol:** 3 attempts per hand, best score.
**What it tells you:** Grip strength is a well-validated proxy for systemic recovery and CNS readiness. A 5–10% rise from Day 1 to Day 7 = deload worked. Flat or down = he's still cooked.
**Cost to recovery:** Zero.

### 3. Vertical Jump or Broad Jump
**Where:** Day 1 (pre-session, after warm-up) and Day 7.
**Protocol:** 3 attempts, best result. Vertical preferred if you have a Vertec or wall mark; broad jump is fine otherwise.
**What it tells you:** Rate-of-force-development proxy. Jumps respond fast to fatigue clearance — a 2–4 cm improvement from Day 1 to Day 7 is a strong "you're ready" signal.
**Cost to recovery:** Negligible. 3 max-effort jumps don't fatigue an advanced lifter.

### 4. Resting Heart Rate & HRV (if he tracks)
**Where:** Every morning, on waking, before phone/coffee.
**What it tells you:** Trending RHR down and HRV up across the week = parasympathetic recovery happening. Flat or worsening = under-recovered going into Week 6.
**Cost to recovery:** Zero.

## What NOT to Test

- ❌ **1RM or 3RM testing** — defeats the entire point of the week.
- ❌ **AMRAP sets** — even at moderate loads, taking sets to failure re-accumulates fatigue.
- ❌ **Rep PRs at submaximal loads** — same issue, just dressed up.
- ❌ **Bench testing this week specifically** — shoulder is a variable, and you don't want pain data confounded with strength data.

## Suggested Tracking Layout

| Day | Marker | Method |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 AM | Grip strength baseline | Dynamometer, 3 attempts/hand |
| Day 1 pre-squat | Vertical jump baseline | 3 attempts, best score |
| Day 1 working sets | Squat bar speed | Film top set of 5 |
| Day 3 working sets | Deadlift bar speed | Film top set of 3 |
| Day 4 working sets | Pull-up bar speed | Film top set of 5 |
| Daily AM | RHR + HRV (if tracked) | Wearable or manual |
| Day 7 AM | Grip strength retest | Same protocol as Day 1 |
| Day 7 | Vertical jump retest | Same protocol as Day 1 |

## Readiness Decision Rule for Week 6

Going into the intensification block, look for **3 of 4** green flags:

1. Grip strength up ≥5% from Day 1 to Day 7
2. Vertical jump up ≥2 cm from Day 1 to Day 7
3. Bar speed at 65% noticeably crisper than Week 4 same-load reps
4. RHR trending down 3–5 bpm across the week

**3 or 4 greens:** Open Week 6 as planned.
**2 greens:** Open Week 6 conservatively — drop opener intensity by ~5%.
**0–1 greens:** Extend deload 3–4 days. Something didn't clear.

## One More Note

Tell him explicitly: **the goal this week is to look weaker on paper while feeling stronger in the body.** If he tries to chase a number on Day 7 to "prove" the deload worked, he's misunderstood it. The proof shows up in Week 6, not Week 5.

I'd push back on this one, and I'd push back hard. Hear me out before you make the call.

## Why "Feeling Great by Wednesday" Is Expected, Not a Signal

Wednesday of a deload is **exactly when** an advanced lifter who just came off 4 weeks at RPE 8.5 should start feeling good. That's the deload working — fatigue is dissipating faster than fitness, which is the entire physiological point (Bannister's fitness-fatigue model, if he wants the textbook version).

**Feeling great mid-deload is not a green light to lift heavier. It's the proof of concept.**

If he ramps Wednesday and Friday, he's not "using" the recovery — he's **spending it** before Week 6 even opens. The intensification block then opens on a lifter who's only partially recovered, and the first heavy session of Week 6 underperforms. I've seen this pattern wreck more good blocks than under-recovery does.

## The Boredom Problem Is Real Though

I take the boredom point seriously — advanced lifters genuinely struggle with sub-threshold weeks, and a bored lifter often sabotages the plan anyway. So rather than push intensity, let's **add psychological stimulus without adding fatigue.** Here's what I'd offer instead:

### Option A — Add Quality, Not Load

Keep the prescribed loads and RPE, but introduce focus points that make sessions feel engaging:

- **Wednesday (Day 3, Posterior Lower):** Add **tempo work** — 4-second eccentric on deadlift, 3-sec pause front squat. Same loads, same sets, but the focus required is high. Feels demanding without being fatiguing.
- **Friday (Day 4, Pull):** Add **execution focus** — film every working set, review between sets, chase perfect bar path on rows and pull-ups. Turn it into a technique session.

### Option B — Add One Power/Speed Element Per Session

Speed work scratches the "I want to do something hard" itch without accumulating fatigue, because the sets are short and far from failure:

- **Wednesday:** Add **3 × 3 speed deadlifts at 60%** before the working sets. Explosive concentric, controlled eccentric. Feels powerful, costs nothing.
- **Friday:** Add **4 × 3 explosive pull-ups** (bodyweight, fast concentric) before working sets.

This is my preferred compromise. He gets to express force, which is what bored advanced lifters are actually craving — not necessarily heavier loads, but *output*.

### Option C — Bring Week 6 Forward by 2 Days

If he genuinely is recovered (and your readiness markers from the tracking protocol back it up by Wednesday — grip up, jump up, RHR down, bar speed crisp), the cleanest move is **not to ramp the deload, but to end it early**. Finish Day 3 as prescribed, take Thursday off, open Week 6 on Friday.

This requires the readiness data to support it. If you don't have green flags by Wednesday, this option is off the table.

## What I'd Specifically Not Do

- ❌ **Push RPE on Wednesday and Friday** — re-introduces the exact fatigue you spent Mon/Tues clearing
- ❌ **Add working sets** — same problem
- ❌ **Let him "test" something heavy** because he feels good — this is the most common deload sabotage and it consistently underdelivers in the next block

## My Recommendation

**Option B (speed work) for Wednesday and Friday.** It gives him output to chase, keeps the deload intact, and actually *primes* the nervous system for Week 6's heavy work — speed work mid-deload is well-established as a peaking tool.

Then **Option C as a fallback:** if by Friday morning his readiness markers are all green and he's still climbing the walls, end the deload Friday and open Week 6 on Saturday or Monday.

If you, knowing the client in the room, decide to override and ramp intensity anyway — I'd cap it at **RPE 7 on Wednesday's main lift only**, hold Friday at RPE 6, and accept that Week 6's opener may need to be dialled back 5%. But that's the concession, not the plan.

What's your read on him — is it genuine readiness, or is it restlessness?

# Week 5 Deload — Summary

## Weekly Layout

| Day | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Lower (Quad) | ~60 min |
| Day 2 | Upper (Push) + Zone 2 30 min | ~60 min + 30 min |
| Day 3 | Lower (Posterior) | ~60 min |
| Day 4 | Upper (Pull) + Zone 2 30 min | ~60 min + 30 min |
| Day 5 | Mobility | 20 min |
| Day 6 | Rest (optional walk) | — |
| Day 7 | Rest | — |

## Volume: Week 5 vs Week 4

| Metric | Week 4 | Week 5 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Working sets / session | 18 | 9 | **–50%** |
| Working sets / week | 72 | 36 | **–50%** |
| Training days | 4 | 4 | unchanged |
| Cardio sessions | per usual | 2 × Zone 2 (30 min) | low aerobic added |
| Mobility | — | 1 × 20 min | added |

## Intensity: Week 5 vs Week 4

| Metric | Week 4 | Week 5 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compound RPE | 8.5 | 6.0 | **–2.5 RPE** |
| Reps in reserve | ~1.5 | ~4 | +2.5 RIR |
| Working load (% of Wk 4 top set) | 100% | 65–70% | **–30–35%** |
| Approx. total tonnage | 100% | ~33% | **–67%** |
| Failure / AMRAP work | present | none | removed |
| Cardio HR zone | n/a | Z2 (60–70% max HR) | low |

## Key Programme Adjustments

# Week 5 Deload — Summary

## Weekly Layout

| Day | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Lower (Quad) | ~60 min |
| Day 2 | Upper (Push) + Zone 2 30 min | ~60 min + 30 min |
| Day 3 | Lower (Posterior) | ~60 min |
| Day 4 | Upper (Pull) + Zone 2 30 min | ~60 min + 30 min |
| Day 5 | Mobility | 20 min |
| Day 6 | Rest (optional walk) | — |
| Day 7 | Rest | — |

## Volume: Week 5 vs Week 4

| Metric | Week 4 | Week 5 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Working sets / session | 18 | 9 | **–50%** |
| Working sets / week | 72 | 36 | **–50%** |
| Training days | 4 | 4 | unchanged |
| Cardio sessions | per usual | 2 × Zone 2 (30 min) | low aerobic added |
| Mobility | — | 1 × 20 min | added |

## Intensity: Week 5 vs Week 4

| Metric | Week 4 | Week 5 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Compound RPE | 8.5 | 6.0 | **–2.5 RPE** |
| Reps in reserve | ~1.5 | ~4 | +2.5 RIR |
| Working load (% of Wk 4 top set) | 100% | 65–70% | **–30–35%** |
| Approx. total tonnage | 100% | ~33% | **–67%** |
| Failure / AMRAP work | present | none | removed |
| Cardio HR zone | n/a | Z2 (60–70% max HR) | low |

## Key Programme Adjustments

- **Bench → Swiss bar / neutral-grip DB press** (cranky shoulder; diagnostic week)
- **Incline press to neutral grip, 30° max** (same logic)
- **OHP flagged** for symptom check; landmine swap on standby
- **No failure, no AMRAPs, no finishers** across all sessions
- **Speed work optional** on Day 3 (deadlift) and Day 4 (pull-up) if boredom becomes a compliance risk

## Readiness Markers Tracked

- Grip strength (Day 1 vs Day 7)
- Vertical jump (Day 1 vs Day 7)
- Bar speed on top sets at 65%
- Resting HR / HRV trend across the week

## Decision Rule for Week 6

**3–4 green markers** → open Week 6 as planned
**2 greens** → open Week 6 at –5% intensity
**0–1 greens** → extend deload 3–4 days

## Bottom Line

Half the volume, two-thirds less tonnage, RPE dropped from grinding to crisp, same movement patterns preserved, shoulder protected, engine ticking over, fatigue clearing — primed to open intensification on Week 6.
